newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ACCESS energy prices ease on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ACCESS energy prices ease on profit-taking.

text.p: NYMEX ACCESS energy prices drifted lower during the first two hours of overnight trade, weakened by ongoing profit-taking.

"It was a continuation of today's weakness," one ACCESS overnight trader said. December crude oil futures fell 67 cents a barrel to $24.86. Traders said prices would keep falling Thursday, with key support at $24.83.
Crude would need to touch $24 a barrel before turning higher, brokers said.
At 1611 PDT, December NYMEX crude traded $24.70 a barrel, down 16 cents from the settle on 1,092 lots traded.
November heating oil, which goes off the board October 31, led losses in daytime and overnight trade, settling 2.49 cents a gallon lower before slipping 0.46 cents further on ACCESS.
At 1611 PDT, November heating oil traded 70.50 cents a gallon on 169 lots exchanged.
"Heat" fell after the American Petroleum Institute released data Tuesday which showed stocks grew 2.4 million barrels for the week ended October 18.
Heavy builds occured in the U.S. Northeast, the world's largest heating oil market, and have risen in recent months on record inventory lows.
Front-month gasoline traded 68.00 cents a gallon in early ACCESS after-hours trade, off 0.16 cent after settling down 0.96 cent. Around 74 lots traded early.

Front-month natural gasoline fell about four cents on ACCESS to $2.530 per million British thermal units, pressured by profit taking. Data from the American Gas Association (AGA) showed Wednesday that U.S. inventory builds were neutral.
